newsitem.title: UK: Faltering freight market takes BFI down again.
newsitem.headline: Faltering freight market takes BFI down again.

text.p: The freight market continued to falter for most categories of tonnage in nearly all areas on Thursday , brokers said.
The Baltic Freight Index lost nine points to 1361, a level not seen for almost three months. The Baltic Handy Index also weakened on a broad front and was down 11 points to 1016.

GRAIN - Grain rates led today's retreat. Bunge lifted subjects on Captain Veniamis, a 1972-built caper of close to five million cft grain, for Mississippi/Holland for Feb 7/12 at a lumpsum equivalent of $10.55 basis light grains.
Last month such business was fixed at $13.00.
Cobelfret took Lemnos, a 20-year old Panamax, for 55,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Ghent at $11.50 for Feb 18/25, two weeks ago these charterers booked Bantry for similar business at $13.00.

Owners also gave ground in the Pacific where Pan Ocean were reported to have fixed Chinese tonnage for 52,500 heavy grain NoPac/S.Korea for mid Feb at $11.50 - yesterday the rate was $12.00, and a fortnight ago $13.25.

Dreyfus covered 50,000 barley NoPac/Saudi Arabia for Feb 7/15 with Thalassini Niki, down 75 cents from the previous fixture reported by Dreyfus on Jan 21, and $1.25 down from the rate fixed on Jan 10.

MINERALS - Bocimar confirmed fixing Georgios M for 110,000 coal Hampton Roads/Le Havre for mid-Feb at $6.30. The BFI panellists accordingly reduced route seven, 110,000 coal Hampton Roads/Rotterdam, from $6.51 yesterday to $6.29 today.
Fertilizer rates from US Gulf to China also fell. There was a report that 50,000 DAP was booked for prompt loading on Spiga at $22.75, business which commanded $24.50 last week.
This latter rate was also reported fixed overnight by Atlantic Fertilizers for Feb 5/10 but basis loading both Tampa and Pascagoula to China.
